# Meat and poultry

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid and total mercury and others, in 1,823 results from 69 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/anses2026-tds3-metals-france|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">ANSES · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/anses2026-tds3-metals-france">Opinion of the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health &amp; </li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Meat and poultry, as sold from wild boar meat content <35% had lead higher at 160 µg/kg, against 100 µg/kg for all samples, 16 brands, Italian market, March-November 2020 in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lenti2021-italy-wild-boar-ragu-lead|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lenti A, Menozzi A, Fedrizzi G, Menotta S, Iemmi T, Galletti G, Serventi P, Bertini S · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lenti2021-italy-wild-boar-ragu-lead">Lead Levels in Wild Boar Meat Sauce (Ragù) Sold on the Italian Market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 2021, 18, 3989</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lenti2021-italy-wild-boar-ragu-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/anses2026-tds3-metals-france|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">ANSES · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/anses2026-tds3-metals-france">Opinion of the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health &amp; Safety on the results of the Third French Total Diet Study (TDS3) - Acrylamide, aluminium, silver, cadmium, mercury and lead</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">ANSES Opinion, Request No 2019-SA-0010</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/anses2026-tds3-metals-france">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/apdraim2023-vermiculite-quail-meat|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Apdraim G, Sarsembayeva N, Lozowicka B · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/apdraim2023-vermiculite-quail-meat">Effect of vermiculite feed additive on the chemical, mineral, and amino acid compositions of quail meat</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/apdraim2023-vermiculite-quail-meat">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2021-keywords-meat-heavy-metal-toxic-elements-health-risk|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2021-keywords-meat-heavy-metal-toxic-elements-health-risk">Keywords: Meat, Heavy metal, Toxic elements, Health risk, Exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2021-keywords-meat-heavy-metal-toxic-elements-health-risk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as meat and poultry

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers meat and poultry in 5 forms kept separate in every comparison: meat and poultry, as sold (1,704 results), meat and poultry, cooked (59 results), meat and poultry, frozen (28 results), meat and poultry, canned (24 results) and meat and poultry, peeled or flesh (8 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-meat" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-meat-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of meat and poultry, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:meat-7954fbd96b3b:c1d732c6f7ed"><summary>HMI meat and poultry Pb reference · Meat and poultry, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:meat-7954fbd96b3b:c1d732c6f7ed"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI meat and poultry Pb reference · Meat and poultry, as sold. Meat and poultry, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>21</td><td>100</td><td>230</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>21</td><td>100</td><td>230–270 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>465 reference units; 5 sampling families. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach meat and poultry

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach meat and poultry comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Meat and poultry, as sold from shot animal 1, sample U1: centre of wound channel, exit side (experiment) had lead higher at 1,960,000 µg/kg, against 97 µg/kg for shot animal 2, control sample U8 in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/qvarfort2025-game-meat-lead-bioaccessibility|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ulf Qvarfort, Christer Holmgren · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/qvarfort2025-game-meat-lead-bioaccessibility">Lead in game meat: a study of bioaccessibility of lead metal fragments</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Analytical Techniques and Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/qvarfort2025-game-meat-lead-bioaccessibility">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, meat and poultry, as sold from Rönnskär (polluted brackish water) (industrial-affected area) had total arsenic higher at 2,600 µg/kg, against 240 µg/kg for Bodaträsk (polluted fresh water) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/norin1985-swedish-fish-arsenic-speciation|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Norin H, Vahter M, Christakopoulos A, Sandstrom M · 1985</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/norin1985-swedish-fish-arsenic-speciation">Concentration of inorganic and total arsenic in fish from industrially polluted water</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemosphere</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/norin1985-swedish-fish-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that meat and poultry, as sold from smoked (processed) cane rat meat from market, uncooked (table: had Mn higher at 5,330 µg/kg, against 1,250 µg/kg for smoked (processed) cane rat meat, then boiled (table: "Processed in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/joyce2016-bush-meat-cooking-ghana|20]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joyce K, Emikpe BO, Asare DA, Asenso TN, Yeboah R, Jarikre TA, Jagun-Jubril A · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/joyce2016-bush-meat-cooking-ghana">Effects of Different Cooking Methods on Heavy Metals Level in Fresh and Smoked Game Meat</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Processing &amp; Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/joyce2016-bush-meat-cooking-ghana">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in meat and poultry?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ag, Ba, <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-meat-and-poultry" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-meat-and-poultry" data-question="How do heavy metals get into meat and poultry?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into meat and poultry?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, meat and poultry from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than meat and poultry from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lenti2021-italy-wild-boar-ragu-lead|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lenti A, Menozzi A, Fedrizzi G, Menotta S, Iemmi T, Galletti G, Serventi P, Bertini S · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lenti2021-italy-wild-boar-ragu-lead">Lead Levels in Wild Boar Meat Sauce (Ragù) Sold on the Italian Market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 2021, 18, 3989</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lenti2021-italy-wild-boar-ragu-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Meat and poultry, as sold from wild boar meat content <35% had lead higher at 160 µg/kg, against 100 µg/kg for all samples, 16 brands, Italian market, March-November 2020 in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lenti2021-italy-wild-boar-ragu-lead|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lenti A, Menozzi A, Fedrizzi G, Menotta S, Iemmi T, Galletti G, Serventi P, Bertini S · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lenti2021-italy-wild-boar-ragu-lead">Lead Levels in Wild Boar Meat Sauce (Ragù) Sold on the Italian Market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 2021, 18, 3989</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lenti2021-italy-wild-boar-ragu-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-meat-and-poultry" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-meat-and-poultry" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in meat and poultry?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in meat and poultry?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, meat and poultry, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (1.19 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (50 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in WPRO (0.412 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (270 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-meat-and-poultry" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-meat-and-poultry" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in meat and poultry?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in meat and poultry?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same meat and poultry.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jamil2015-lahore-chicken-goat-cow-organs-metals|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jamil N, Baqar M, Manzoor M, Abbas N, Qadir A, Ahsan N, Shaikh IA, Munir S, Arslan M, Zahid H · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jamil2015-lahore-chicken-goat-cow-organs-metals">Accumulation of Heavy Metals in Edible Organs of Different Meat Products Available in the Markets of Lahore, Pakistan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Pakistan Journal of Scientific and Industrial Research Series B: Biological Sciences 58(2):92-97</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jamil2015-lahore-chicken-goat-cow-organs-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Meat and poultry, peeled or flesh (Lahore markets (5 markets pooled)) had lead higher at 1,120 µg/kg, against 698 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (meat and poultry, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/jamil2015-lahore-chicken-goat-cow-organs-metals|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jamil N, Baqar M, Manzoor M, Abbas N, Qadir A, Ahsan N, Shaikh IA, Munir S, Arslan M, Zahid H · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jamil2015-lahore-chicken-goat-cow-organs-metals">Accumulation of Heavy Metals in Edible Organs of Different Meat Products Available in the Markets of Lahore, Pakistan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Pakistan Journal of Scientific and Industrial Research Series B: Biological Sciences 58(2):92-97</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jamil2015-lahore-chicken-goat-cow-organs-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-meat-and-poultry-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-meat-and-poultry-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in meat and poultry is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in meat and poultry is inorganic?</summary>
